name: pulse-state-effects
description: Designs React state, effects, refs, memoization, subscriptions, cleanup, and hydration-safe render logic for components in this Laravel Inertia React 19 app. Use when local state, effects, subscriptions, browser stores, refs, memoization, or hydration-safe rendering decisions are needed.
purpose: Avoid derived state bugs, effect misuse, stale closures, hydration mismatches, and unnecessary renders.
single_responsibility: React component state mechanics: state shape and ownership, effects and cleanup, refs, memoization, external stores, and hydration-safe render.
triggers: Component needs local state, effects, subscriptions, timers, observers, or refs
Hydration mismatch risk exists at the server/client boundary
Memoization, external browser stores, or event-handler vs effect decisions are needed
A custom hook is being extracted
completion_criteria: State shape and ownership are decided and kept minimal
Derived state is computed during render, not duplicated
Effects have narrow dependencies and clean up timers, frames, observers, requests, and listeners
Initial render is deterministic with no browser-only branches
Memoization is applied only for real cost or identity boundaries
validation_criteria: Hook extraction remains reusable and typed
failure_handling: If a deterministic first render cannot be achieved or an effect cannot be made safe, stop and report the hydration or effect risk instead of suppressing warnings or shipping non-deterministic render.
Report any state, effect, or cleanup decision left unresolved because behaviour or SSR context is unknown.
escalation_path: Route uncertain React 19, hydration, or external-store API behaviour through pulse-docs-research.
Hand public API and prop shape concerns to pulse-api-contract and broader render-cost review to pulse-performance-vercel.
Escalate to the user when fixing state behaviour requires a scope or dependency change.
responsibilities: Use `useSyncExternalStore` for external browser stores when needed.
Treat React `memo`, `useMemo`, and `useCallback` as targeted tools for real cost or identity boundaries.
